tasks.title: Task by task
tasks.intro: The {n, integer} tasks that fill a typical week, largest first. Open a task to see the evidence and the arithmetic behind its category.
tasks.more: {n, integer} more tasks O*NET lists for this job
tasks.moreNote: Rarer or less important, so the typical week leaves them out. Your own week can include them.
tasks.ratingSource_human+gpt4: researchers and GPT-4 disagreed, so we use the mean

explain.observed_auto: Seen in real AI use at work: {auto} of the conversations about this task in {source} hand the whole task to AI.
explain.observed_collab: Seen in real AI use at work: in {collab} of the conversations about this task in {source}, people work on it together with AI rather than handing it over.
explain.personal_use: Published in AI usage data, but only {work} of that use is work, so it does not count as observed work use. The research rating was {label}.
explain.estimate_e1: Not seen in published AI work use yet. Researchers rated it E1: a language model alone can halve the time.
explain.estimate_e2: Not seen in published AI work use yet. Researchers rated it E2: AI can halve the time with extra tools built around it.
explain.estimate_e0: Not seen in published AI work use yet. Researchers rated it E0: a language model barely helps.
explain.estimate_dwa: No direct rating, so we use the average of tasks with the same detailed work activity ({theory}).
explain.physical: A physical, hands-on task with no sign of AI use anywhere. It stays with people.
explain.no_data: No research rating and no observed use yet.
explain.earlier_use: Not in the latest work-use data, but it showed up in an earlier release of the Anthropic Economic Index, so AI already helps with it.
explain.penetration: Researchers rated it low, but Anthropic's own measure finds AI use for it ({penetration} task penetration), so AI already helps with it.
explain.estimate_mixed: Not seen in published AI work use yet. Researchers rated it {human} and GPT-4 rated it {gpt4}, so we take the middle ({theory}).
